text:
### Observed differences

- A set of activities that runs in every case — A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26, with A31 and A32 also present in nearly every case — was flexibly ordered in the earlier window and is executed in one fixed order in the later window. Earlier, A24 preceded A20 in about 73 in 100 cases and preceded A23 in about 88 in 100, while A20–A26 and A22–A24 each appeared in both orders roughly half the time; in the later window A20 precedes A24 in about 99 in 100 cases, A23 precedes A24 in about 97, A20 precedes A26 in about 98, and A22 precedes A24 in about 99. [REL014, REL016, REL017, REL019, LAG031, LAG026]
- The distances between these activities became fixed as well. In the earlier window, gaps spread over two to five events — for example, A22 reached A23 anywhere from two to five events later, A24 reached A25 over two to five events, and A31 reached A24 immediately in only about half of the cases. In the later window each pair sits at one distance almost always: A31→A22, A22→A20 and A20→A23 one event apart (about 995–1000 in 1000), A22→A23 and A24→A25 two events apart (about 995 in 1000), A23→A25 three events apart (essentially always), and A31→A24 four events apart (about 995 in 1000). [LAG006, LAG011, LAG012, LAG016, LAG021, LAG032, LAG033, LAG034]
- Event positions corroborate this reordering: in the later window A20, A22 and A23 sit slightly earlier in the case (mean position about 0.64→0.59, 0.60→0.57 and 0.69→0.62) while A24 and A26 sit slightly later (about 0.60→0.65 and 0.64→0.67); all five still occur in every case in both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- A08 became much rarer: it appeared in about 72 in 100 cases before and in about 29 in 100 in the later window (mean occurrences per trace 0.75→0.32). When it does occur, it sits later and far more variably (mean position about 0.24→0.41, 75th percentile about 0.24→0.69), and its earlier habit of immediately preceding A16 (one event apart in about 99 in 100 of the observed pairs) largely dissolved, with about 43 in 100 now adjacent and the rest spread out to five events. [OCC001, POS001, LAG001]
- A10 appeared in about 8 in 100 cases before and about 22 in 100 in the later window; this rests on only 15 versus 44 traces, so the shift is modestly supported. [OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the always-executed core of the process — A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26, anchored by A31 and A32 — moved from flexibly ordered execution with variable gaps to a single fixed sequence: the order and gap data are mutually consistent with a chain A31 → A22 → A20 → A23 → A24 → A26 → A25 → A32 in which consecutive activities sit one event apart (the final step to A32 holding in about 90 in 100 cases), whereas in the earlier window the same pairs ran in mixed or reversed orders at varying distances. [REL014, REL016, REL017, REL019, LAG006, LAG011, LAG012, LAG021, LAG022, LAG026, LAG029]

This reading is direct and consistent: the order and gap changes are measured on pairs that co-occur in 100 in 100 cases in both windows, roughly eight order relations and more than a dozen gap distributions point the same way, and the screening flagged 67 items against an expectation of 0.76 without change (control-flow family, 153 units tested) — a count far beyond what an unchanged process produces. Limitations: distances are counted in event steps, not clock time; the exact chain is a consistent reading rather than a directly measured path, since not every adjacent pair was tested; and qualifying items resting on only 1–13 later-window observations were excluded from the argument. [LAG002, LAG019, LAG024, LAG027, LAG037]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the earlier window mixed several coexisting orderings and the later window is dominated by one of them; the data show that the executed behaviour became fixed, but cannot tell whether the other orderings were removed or merely absent from this sample. [REL016, REL017]

Other differences: A08 was executed far less often in the later window (about 29 in 100 cases versus about 72 before), sits later and more variably when present, and no longer immediately precedes A16 in most cases; A10 participation rose from about 8 to about 22 in 100 cases on modest counts. These are participation changes and are kept separate from the ordering hypothesis above. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, LAG001]
